name: getrusage
description: getrusage() retrieves resource usage statistics for a specified entity, such as the calling process, its children, or the calling thread. It stores the information in a struct rusage, which includes metrics like CPU time and memory usage.

parameters.name: who
parameters.description: Specifies the entity for which to retrieve resource usage: RUSAGE_SELF for the calling process, RUSAGE_CHILDREN for terminated children, or RUSAGE_THREAD for the calling thread (available since Linux 2.6.26).

parameters.name: usage
parameters.description: Pointer to a struct rusage where the resource usage data is stored, including fields like ru_utime and ru_stime.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: usage points outside the accessible address space

bugs: Before Linux 2.6.9, if the disposition of SIGCHLD was set to SIG_IGN, resource usages of child processes were incorrectly included in RUSAGE_CHILDREN, contrary to POSIX; this was fixed in Linux 2.6.9 and later. Not all fields in struct rusage are maintained and are set to zero.
